When Donald Trump isn't busy [destroying the White House to build a highly
corrupt ballroom](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-white-house-ballroom-food-health)
or [starting illegal wars](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-iran-war-pentagon-good-
news), he's excited about all his party-planning ahead of the Fourth of July.

For months, two Trump advisers tell **Zeteo** , the U.S. president has
actively involved himself in the minutiae of the planning and pageantry for
events during and leading up to the United States Semiquincentennial, the
250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence's adoption.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

The president has been briefed many times on things like events details, the
roster of booked celebrity appearances, pyrotechnics, military spectacle, and
other logistics, and has enthusiastically proposed his own ideas. Trump has
told advisers that it'll be a great "party" between now and the July 4
festivities in Washington, D.C., and he's taken a special interest in facets
such as the days of musical performances, and the upcoming [UFC
fights](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/05/29/pentagon-
recruiting-troops-watch-white-house-ufc-fights-memos-show/) in front of the
White House marking Trump's birthday.

But this week, something went wrong - and now President Trump's big "party"
might not be so great after all.
